scope: RF-domain capture/qualification/upload/replay soft-reset sequencing, not complete board reset
request: Synchronous clk_rf level; even a one-cycle request is retained. Requests while busy coalesce into the active reset, not a queue.
admission: block_new_work asserts combinationally with reset_request and remains asserted until completion and request deassertion. Gate new joint capture/context/replay admissions; continue all already admitted work.

drain_proofs.producers_idle: No admitted sample window, EOP, statistics, noise or delayed producer result remains. Must come from producer ownership tracking.
drain_proofs.qualification_idle: No retained qualification context, pipeline result, bank commit or pending publication event; qualification_publish_bridge.idle covers its maps.
drain_proofs.upload_idle: No accepted descriptor or RAM upload read remains; capture_record_system.idle_rf. Does not assert FIFO empty or host delivery.
drain_proofs.replay_idle: No replay task/read/return remains. Upstream stops new replay work and proves all pending work complete.

sequence: Require all four proofs high on two consecutive DRAIN edges. Then assert owner_reset_request and wait for owner_epoch == previous_epoch + 1 modulo 2^64. done pulses once. Hold owner_reset_request until external request has deasserted.
no_timeout_discard: Never force reset while a drain proof is missing. Permanent downstream stall or missing producer result leaves busy asserted and requires diagnosis; no silent RAW loss.
integration_requirements: All inputs and proofs already synchronous to clk_rf
Do not tie block_new_work to qualification quiesce, sample_valid, existing-result valid or upload ready
Only the coordinator drives the capture owner soft-reset request
Once drain is proved, no new producer/reader work may appear before RUN resumes
Keep upload FIFO and clk_mem alive: this soft reset does not discard already queued bytes
Hard rst requires external DMA isolation and both-domain quiescence and is outside this protocol
Full-system producer tracking, admission arbitration and physical-top connections remain to be implemented
